question:
Charlotte the spider is walking along a web shaped like a \(5\)-pointed star, shown in the figure below. The web has \(5\) outer points and \(5\) inner points. Each time Charlotte reaches a point, she randomly chooses a neighboring point and moves to that point. Charlotte starts at one of the outer points and makes \(3\) moves (re-visiting points is allowed). What is the probability she is now at one of the outer points of the star?

[Figure 1](figures/2026_AMC_8_Q21_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
We only need to track whether Charlotte is at an inner or outer point, because all points of the same type have the same numbers of each type of neighbor.

[Figure 1](figures/2026_AMC_8_Q21_question_fig1.svg)

Each outer point has two neighbors, both inner. Each inner point has four neighbors: two inner and two outer. Thus, from any inner point, Charlotte has probability \(\frac12\) of moving to either type.

Charlotte starts at an outer point, so her first move certainly takes her to an inner point. After her second move, she has probability \(\frac12\) of being inner and probability \(\frac12\) of being outer.

On the third move, every route that was at an outer point moves to an inner point. Of the probability already at inner points, half moves to outer points. These two cases cover every possible route, so the requested probability is
\[
\frac12\cdot\frac12=\boxed{\frac14}.
\]
The answer is \(\text{B}\).

Method 1: Track inner and outer points

\[
\frac12\cdot\frac12=\boxed{\frac14}.

The answer is \(\text{B}\).

answerCheck.reason: Let p_n be the probability of being at an outer point after n moves. The neighbor counts give p_(n+1)=(1-p_n)/2. Starting with p_0=1 gives p_1=0, p_2=1/2, and p_3=1/4.

nodes.description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number , e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem. For example, if each person at a party will eat 3/8 of a pound of roast beef, and there will be 5 people at the party, how many pounds of roast beef will be needed? nodes.description: Interpret the product (a/b) × q as a parts of a partition of q into b equal parts; equivalently, as the result of a sequence of operations a × q ÷ b.
